DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.
